concept: Measuring ANN recall against ENN baselines
summary: Source-anchored research for Measuring ANN recall against ENN baselines. Run status: COMPLETED.

facts.text: High ANN recall establishes fidelity to exact vector neighbors, not semantic relevance or end-to-end output quality. Qdrant separates these evaluation layers, and Elastic distinguishes mathematical recall from relevance. (high confidence) Sources: https://qdrant.tech/documentation/tutorials-search-engineering/ann-recall/ ; https://www.elastic.co/search-labs/blog/recall-vector-search-quantization

The June 3, 2026 preprint ANN Search: Recall What Matters argues that using Recall@k to assess retrieval quality forces unnecessary computational overhead, because what matters is the quality of retrieved results rather than overlap with the true kNN set. Its abstract reports downstream indicators remaining highly stable even when Recall@k drops significantly, and proposes 1/Ratio@k, the inverse approximation ratio, which evaluates differences between distances of retrieved and true neighbors, as a more accurate proxy; this is a research finding, not a universal replacement rule. Sources: https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.04522

Use exhaustive exact search as the reference and run ANN with the same query criteria. MongoDB's worked comparison preserves the query vector, vector field, filter and result limit; Elastic's demonstration compares optimized search with a full-Float32 flat-search reference. (medium confidence) Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/query/improve-accuracy.md ; https://www.elastic.co/search-labs/blog/recall-vector-search-quantization

Increasing numCandidates in an ANN query makes results a closer match to ENN results, but consumes additional computational resources and might reduce query speed. Faiss similarly frames tuning as finding the best search time for a given accuracy. Comparing configurations at a common recall target is an evaluation recommendation, not measured savings. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/query/improve-accuracy.md ; https://engineering.fb.com/2017/03/29/data-infrastructure/faiss-a-library-for-efficient-similarity-search/

Use representative workload queries rather than a single example. MongoDB recommends a set of 100 example queries; Qdrant describes a typically 20–50 query sample. These are tutorial sample sizes, not statistical guarantees that production tails are covered. (high confidence) Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/query/improve-accuracy.md ; https://qdrant.tech/documentation/tutorials-search-engineering/ann-recall/

The inspected ANN-Benchmarks implementation counts returned distances within the exact kth-neighbor distance plus a default epsilon of 0.001, then averages the count divided by k. This distance-tolerant measure can differ from strict ID overlap; declare the evaluator and tolerance when comparing benchmark results. (low confidence)

Evaluate a representative set of queries rather than treating one successful query as evidence of overall recall. Both MongoDB and Qdrant describe multi-query comparisons and aggregated overlap evaluation. (medium confidence) Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/query/improve-accuracy.md ; https://qdrant.tech/documentation/tutorials-search-engineering/ann-recall/index.md

Faiss evaluates the trade-off between speed and accuracy for a fixed memory usage, and its automatic tuning collects operating points giving the best possible search time given some accuracy. Comparing speed and memory at a shared accuracy target for TCO is an inference from this framing, not a methodology Faiss prescribes. Sources: https://engineering.fb.com/2017/03/29/data-infrastructure/faiss-a-library-for-efficient-similarity-search/
Construct ENN ground truth with exhaustive similarity evaluation, then compare ANN results for the same query criteria. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/query/improve-accuracy.md

For two full top-k result sets, ID-overlap recall@k is |ANN_k intersect ENN_k| / k. Average it across test queries; nine shared IDs out of ten means recall@10 = 0.9. This set metric does not evaluate ranking within those shared IDs. (high confidence)

Jaccard similarity is intersection divided by union, whereas top-k overlap recall divides by k. For equal-sized top-k sets with overlap m, Jaccard = m/(2k-m), so recall = 2J/(1+J). Nine shared results at k=10 yield recall 0.9 but Jaccard about 0.818; this conversion follows algebraically from the cited definitions. (high confidence) Sources: https://docs.scipy.org/doc/scipy/reference/generated/scipy.spatial.distance.jaccard.html ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/query/improve-accuracy.md ; https://www.elastic.co/search-labs/blog/recall-vector-search-quantization

Elastic explicitly scopes its recall example as a very small-scale demonstration and advises testing on the user’s own data. Its example is not evidence that Atlas and separate infrastructure meet identical recall, latency or cost requirements at production scale. (low confidence)

Increasing search effort trades resources and latency for closer agreement with exact results: MongoDB discusses increasing numCandidates, and Qdrant discusses increasing hnsw_ef. Measure the resulting recall and latency together. (medium confidence) Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/query/improve-accuracy.md ; https://qdrant.tech/documentation/tutorials-search-engineering/ann-recall/index.md

The June 3, 2026 preprint ANN Search: Recall What Matters reports that downstream classification and RAG quality can remain stable while Recall@k falls, and proposes inverse approximation ratio as an alternative utility proxy. This is a research finding, not a universal replacement rule; only its abstract was inspected. (low confidence)
